subject: Aurora University — DPF & DPA annex: technical evidence and follow-up
messages:
From: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@aurora.edu>
To: connor.obrien@redwood.ai
Cc: dpo@aurora.edu
Date: 2028-06-28T14:12:00-04:00
Subject: Aurora University: DPF supplement and DPA annex questions

Hi Connor,

Thanks again for the overview earlier this month. Aurora's procurement & privacy teams reviewed the initial materials and have a set of follow-up requests we need in order to close the security/privacy gate for the platform evaluation. We're consolidating answers for our internal legal review by end of day Friday (6/30). Can you confirm you can provide the items below by then?

1) DPF/Transfer Mechanism: Confirm the mechanism(s) Redwood relies on for transfers of Aurora EU-origin personal data to the US (SCCs, DPF, other). If relying on DPF, provide the DPF legal opine or summary of coverage and where it is maintained.
2) DPA Annex: We need a redlined processor DPA annex that aligns with our controller requirements (data retention, deletion on termination, subprocessors, audit rights).
3) Subprocessors: Current list (name + country + purpose) and the process/timing for notifying customers of changes.
4) Technical & Organizational Controls: Network topology for the hosted inference environment, encryption (at-rest and in-transit) specifics, key custody model (KMS/HSM or customer-managed), and log retention & access controls for auditable telemetry.
5) Evidence: SOC2-type report (or equivalent), relevant penetration test summaries, and any transfer-assurance packs you maintain for education-sector controllers.
6) Data Residency options: Can you provide details on routing/pinning options to keep processing in-region or guaranteed regional isolation for our student records workloads?

We attached a short checklist (we'll send separately) and can share our DPA annex if that's helpful. If you can't meet 6/30, please propose the earliest alternate date. Also, could we schedule a 30-minute technical Q&A tomorrow (6/29) with your infra/security SME?

Thanks,
Angela Ruiz
Head of Procurement
Aurora University

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Aurora's checklist. High priority: legal needs a redline back to them by EOD Fri and infra needs to assemble a network diagram + subprocessors export. Quick asks below —

Marissa: Can you prepare a redline of our Processor DPA that:
- Confirms deletion obligations and an explicit data return/destruction clause on termination,
- Confirms audit rights limited to agreed scope with notice,
- Adds a controlled subprocessor approval & post-notification model (they may insist on prior approval; propose approach).

Ben: Please export the current subprocessor table (name/country/purpose) and produce a PNG of the hosted topology showing network segmentation, KMS model (we generally use AWS KMS + customer-managed keys for Private), and token/key handling for inference KV caches. Also include retention windows for logs and where audit logs are stored and how they can be shared for compliance review.

I'll coordinate the consolidated response and call scheduling. If either of you foresee any blockers meeting the 6/30 deadline, flag now.

—Connor
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-29T09:40:00-04:00

On Thu, Jun 28, 2028 at 4:08 PM Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Marissa / Ben — forwarding Aurora's checklist. High priority: legal needs a redline back to them by EOD Fri and infra needs to assemble a network diagram + subprocessors export. Quick asks below —

Connor — attaching a redlined DPA (dpa-annex-redline-aurora-2028.docx). Key points I revised / recommended:

1) Deletion & Return: Added explicit language that Redwood will, at controller's direction, return or securely delete personal data within 60 days of termination, with certificate of deletion for the Aurora account.
2) Subprocessors: Proposed a hybrid approval/notification approach: for high-risk subprocessor categories (hosting, KMS, telemetry analytics) require prior written approval; for low-risk operational subprocessors use 30-day post-notification. This is a compromise that is typically acceptable to enterprise education customers.
3) Audit Rights: Clarified scope to preserve Redwood's operational security while offering on-site or remote audits annually with reasonable notice and a narrow scope (controls & evidence relevant to Aurora's processing).
4) Encryption & Keys: Inserted clause confirming encryption in-transit (TLS1.2+) and at-rest, and options for customer-managed keys for Private deployments (we can provide BYOK options).

I left comment flags for the DPF language (Connor — see comments where we should summarize our DPF reliance model rather than include the full legal opine in the DPA).

Ben — please put your subprocessor list and topology PNG into the shared drive folder. I can then pull a short excerpt for the DPF supplement and include an appendix in the redline.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
